legend: The king of Berland organizes a ball! n%%ZSMJ0%% pair are invited to the ball, they are numbered from 1%%ZSMJ1%% to n%%ZSMJ2%%. Each pair consists of one man and one woman. Each dancer (either man or woman) has a monochrome costume. The color of each costume is represented by an integer from 1%%ZSMJ3%% to k%%ZSMJ4%%, inclusive.

Let bi%%ZSMJ5%% be the color of the man's costume and gi%%ZSMJ6%% be the color of the woman's costume in the i%%ZSMJ7%%-th pair. You have to choose a color for each dancer's costume (i.e. values b1,b2,…,bn%%ZSMJ8%% and g1,g2,…gn%%ZSMJ9%%) in such a way that:
for every i%%ZSMJ10%%: bi%%ZSMJ11%% and gi%%ZSMJ12%% are integers between 1%%ZSMJ13%% and k%%ZSMJ14%%, inclusive;
there are no two completely identical pairs, i.e. no two indices i,j%%ZSMJ15%% (i≠j%%ZSMJ16%%) such that bi=bj%%ZSMJ17%% and gi=gj%%ZSMJ18%% at the same time;
there is no pair such that the color of the man's costume is the same as the color of the woman's costume in this pair, i.e. bi≠gi%%ZSMJ19%% for every i%%ZSMJ20%%;

for each two consecutive (adjacent) pairs both man's costume colors and woman's costume colors differ, i.e. for every i%%ZSMJ21%% from 1%%ZSMJ22%% to n−1%%ZSMJ23%% the conditions bi≠bi+1%%ZSMJ24%% and gi≠gi+1%%ZSMJ25%% hold.
Let's take a look at the examples of bad and good color choosing (for n=4%%ZSMJ26%% and k=3%%ZSMJ27%%, man is the first in a pair and woman is the second):
(1,2)%%ZSMJ28%%, (2,3)%%ZSMJ29%%, (3,2)%%ZSMJ30%%, (1,2)%%ZSMJ31%% — contradiction with the second rule (there are equal pairs);
(2,3)%%ZSMJ32%%, (1,1)%%ZSMJ33%%, (3,2)%%ZSMJ34%%, (1,3)%%ZSMJ35%% — contradiction with the third rule (there is a pair with costumes of the same color);
(1,2)%%ZSMJ36%%, (2,3)%%ZSMJ37%%, (1,3)%%ZSMJ38%%, (2,1)%%ZSMJ39%% — contradiction with the fourth rule (there are two consecutive pairs such that colors of costumes of men/women are the same).
You have to find any suitable color choosing or say that no suitable choosing exists.
input: The only line of the input contains two integers n%%ZSMJ52%% and k%%ZSMJ53%% (2≤n,k≤2⋅105%%ZSMJ54%%) — the number of pairs and the number of colors.
output: If it is impossible to find any suitable colors choosing, print "NO".

Otherwise print "YES" and then the colors of the costumes of pairs in the next n%%ZSMJ55%% lines. The i%%ZSMJ56%%-th line should contain two integers bi%%ZSMJ57%% and gi%%ZSMJ58%% — colors of costumes of man and woman in the i%%ZSMJ59%%-th pair, respectively.
You can print each letter in any case (upper or lower). For example, "YeS", "no" and "yES" are all acceptable.
